s: beryllium; the chemical element and alkaline earth metal with the atomic number 4
Beryllium.et: Beryll + Latin -ium, first used by Friedrich Wöhler in 1828.

Beryll.et: Learned borrowing from Latin bēryllus. Doublet of Brille, a borrowing from Old French.

s: Berytus (an ancient city in modern-day Lebanon, now Beirut)
Berytus.et: From Latin Bērȳtus, from Ancient Greek Βηρῡτός (Bērūtós), from Phoenician 𐤁𐤓𐤕 (brt). Doublet of Beirut.

s: Berytian (native or inhabitant of ancient Berytus (modern Beirut))
